rationale:
Pillars v3 (round 2) merges the five designs into one set of exactly 100 pillars. It meets the owner requirements of 2026-11-13 and the owner's relayed instruction: "go, bitcoin in at 5%, options-income in, 60k cap fine". This revision fixes the two blocking problems and the other audit findings from round 1.

Split (target 25/10/20/25/10/10, met exactly):
- news and events: 25 (NWS01-NWS17 market news, plus 8 structural EVT pillars). All 25 now score each mapped fund group or sleeve from -2 to +2 with dated sources, logged weekly in runs/news_log.csv. The EVT pillars also keep their 0-3 severity, which is the gate and S1 trigger. EVT09's group score is an execution-window score (only -1 or 0). It is logged but kept out of the news view N and out of the primary REC08 test, because it forecasts order-day friction, not 1-3 month returns. That is the one stated nuance on requirement 1.
- macro regime: 10 (MAC01-MAC10, all computed by code);
- line choice and safety: 20 (ELG 8, CST 6, TAX 3, DUR 3, down from 33 by merging near-duplicates);
- exposure, valuation and risk: 25 (EXR 6, FAC 6, RSK 5, CON 3, OPT 4, BTC 1);
- fit with the owner's mix: 10 (FIT);
- record and testing: 10 (REC).

US universe count, a small stated deviation from "about 150": round 2 adds four products to the information-only list. They are BTCI (bitcoin-linked, so it would bypass the 5% bitcoin cap), SVOL (short VIX futures), YMAX (a fund of single-stock option-income ETFs) and ULTY (option income on a few single stocks). That leaves 145 US-listed buy candidates (168 unique US tickers minus 23 information-only). It is still about 150, and the four would break owner requirement 4 if they were buyable.

What does not change:
- The owner's strategic mix (config/portfolio_v2.yaml) routes every deposit to the sleeve furthest below target, and it is the yardstick.
- Structural events act at once.
- Scores and news move no deposit money until a pre-registered rule beats the mix in the gate (DECISION_RULES_V2 section 2). Scores use REC04. News uses REC08's single primary test first, then the REC04 standard.

The evidence all designs agree on:
- Rotation lost to holding. In runs/backtest_latest.json (2015-2026, monthly deposits), holding VT returned 11.85% money-weighted. Weekly top-5 returned 5.71%, monthly top-5 8.68% and weekly top-1 2.79%. Momentum switching returned 14.42%, but with a 49.7% drawdown against 32.6% for holding, and it lost about 6% a year in 2015-2019.
- REC04: score tilts lose to the v2 mix (information ratio -0.24 and -0.21, deflated probability 0.00-0.001). This result was measured against the 70/20/10 mix and must be re-run against the new 66.5/19/9.5/5 mix and the cross-wrapper groups before v3 cites it.
- REC07: the 70/20/10 mix returned 11.2% against 9.9% for 100% world (2003-2026), with a similar worst drop.
- Macro predictors fail out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008). Media tone moves prices briefly and then partly reverses (Tetlock 2007).
So macro is context and guardrails only. News is a large, logged, forward-tested category, never a backtested decision driver.

Main choices:
1. Same-index groups span wrappers (ELG07) and count once.
   - Membership comes from declared benchmark identity, not from a return correlation. Measured on 2026-11-13, weekly correlations across London and New York stay below 0.98 even for identical indices (CSPX.L/VOO 0.93), and even for two share classes of one fund on one exchange (JEPG.L/JEGA.L 0.89). Monthly correlations pass 0.95 (CSPX.L/VOO 0.965, VWRA.L/VT 0.965, CNDX.L/QQQ 0.982, JEPQ.L/JEPQ 0.985, JEPI.L/JEPI 0.976, BTCW.L/IBIT 0.993).
   - The return check is therefore monthly with a threshold of 0.95 across venues. Failing it flags a line for review but never splits a benchmark-identical group.
2. One line-choice formula across wrappers (CST10).
   - US-listed lines always carry 30% investor withholding on ordinary distributions (no US-UAE treaty; IRC 871(a), 1441). Irish UCITS carry the 15% look-through inside the fund.
   - When CST02 is missing, every group uses the fallback TERnow + TAX01 + entry cost. Nothing fails closed for lack of ter_history.
   - The comparisons now use true same-strategy twins: VOO about 35 bps against CSPX 23.5; VT about 53 against VWRA 24.6; QQQM about 29 against XNAS 33.4 (inside the hurdle); JEPI about 273 against JEPI.L about 55; JEPQ about 394 against JEPQ.L about 45.
   - The UCITS figures are TER plus the 15% look-through on an assumed stock dividend yield of about 1.5% for JEPI.L and 0.7% for JEPQ.L. ELN coupons are assumed to carry no US withholding.
3. The US$60,000 US-situs cap (FIT12, S8) has bands at 45k and 54k and a switch at 60k. It fails closed for buying: no US-situs order until ibkr_entity, w8ben_signed_on and positions_as_of are recorded.
4. Bitcoin: speculative, owner target 5%, and 5% is now a true cap.
   - Buys never take B above 5%.
   - At every month-end check, once the deposit has been routed elsewhere, B above 5.0% is trimmed to 4.5% (S7). The trim is always at least 0.5% of the portfolio, which keeps its commission share falling as the portfolio grows.
   - Bitcoin orders need at least US$340, so the US$1.70 commission stays at or below 0.5%. A smaller gap is carried. Below a portfolio of about US$6,800 there is no bitcoin buy.
   - The owner may choose a 4.5% target instead to reduce churn; the cap stays 5%.
   - The preferred line is a physically backed LSE ETP. These are secured ETNs, not ETFs. They are not US-situs, but they need the owner's crypto-ETP permission and a TER seeded from the KID before any order. If they cannot be ordered, the sleeve uses a US spot ETF inside FIT12 headroom.
5. Options-income (the O view) is rescaled so it is no longer saturated.
   - OPT01 scores upside given up against the plain buy-write of the same underlying (BXM 0.56, BXN 0.44) and against the line's own beta. Measured: JEPQ up-capture 0.73 at beta 0.66; QYLD 0.52 at beta 0.51. JEPQ scores about 84 and QYLD about 59.
   - OPT02 scores net income against peers on the same underlying, not against the index dividend yield.
   - OPT03 uses beta-adjusted down-capture plus the beta-matched net return gap.
   - The gate is now that a line's O must be at least the O of the plain buy-write proxy.
   - The sleeve target stays 0 until the owner answers an explicit prompt: target (10% proposed), underlying, and which sleeve it comes from. REC07 variant (b) shows the cost beside the prompt: BXM trailed the S&P 500 by 3.75 points a year and BXN trailed the Nasdaq-100 by 10.2.
6. Never bought (information only): leveraged, inverse, single-stock (TSLY, NVDY, MSTY, CONY), concentrated single-stock baskets (ULTY, YMAX), buffer, volatility (SVOL), futures-crypto and bitcoin-linked income (BTCI), US partnerships and unsecured ETNs.
7. News: 25 lead agents choose explorer counts above a floor and the number of rounds until saturation. Every weekly per-group score goes to a hash-chained ledger. Display only until the single pre-registered REC08 primary test passes.
8. X keeps v2's weights exactly. Before v3 claims that the REC04 result still stands, REC04 and REC07 are re-run against the new yardstick mix and the cross-wrapper groups.

Source labels were corrected: FIT01, FIT12, FIT13, CON04, NWS14, REC03 and EXR06 are unverified until their inputs exist. MAC05 uses CNY=X in place of CNH=X, which returns no data. MAC04's term premium is labelled Kim-Wright. Cboe files are fetched with redirects followed.

families.name: Market news by fund group (agents, expanding rounds)
families.purpose: News view N, a separate view (neutral = 50). Seventeen topic pillars cover every market topic the owner listed. Each has a lead agent that chooses topics, explorer counts (above a floor) and the number of rounds until its topic is saturated. Each pillar scores its mapped fund groups from -2 to +2 for the next 1-3 months, with confidence and at least 2 dated sources. Every weekly score is logged append-only in runs/news_log.csv. N per group combines the 17 NWS scores and the group scores of EVT01, EVT02 and EVT04-EVT08. EVT09 is excluded because it is an execution score. Each fact is owned by one pillar, so it is counted once. Display and record only: N moves no deposit money until the pre-registered REC08 primary test passes and then the REC04 standard against the owner's mix. It never sells (S0).

families.name: Structural, fund-level and owner-level events (agents)
families.purpose:
Eight agent pillars use the same expanding-round machinery as NWS. They cover fund corporate actions, fees and substitutes, index changes, issuer and custodian health, tax and legal changes for a UAE resident, sanctions and market access, the broker and funding channel, and the deposit-week calendar. Each writes two outputs:
(1) severity 0-3 per line or issuer, with a primary source required for 2 or more. This is the gate and the S1, S6 or S8 trigger, and acts at once without any backtest;
(2) a per-group or per-sleeve score from -2 to +2 in runs/news_log.csv under the REC08 fields, from a pre-registered map. Adverse severity 1, 2 or 3 gives -1, -2 or -2. A confirmed favourable event gives +1: a fee cut, a cheaper same-index substitute, a new UCITS twin, a better access route, or less concentration. A material favourable rule change confirmed by T1 plus T2 sources gives +2. Otherwise 0. EVT09 scores only -1 or 0, for an order-window conflict.
Line view: EVT is 7 of 100 (CST 50, TAX 24, DUR 19, EVT 7), penalty-only from the severities of EVT01, EVT02 and EVT05 in equal thirds, scored 50/40/25/0.

families.name: Macro regime (computed)
families.purpose: Ten code-computed regime readings from verified FRED and yfinance series. Each has raw values with release dates, a percentile against its own history, one pre-registered flag, and a cached last-good fallback with an age flag. Weight 0 in every view, because macro predictors fail out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008). Uses: execution caution (MAC03); the sale-freeze and drawdown-protocol guardrails (MAC09); owner context for the diversifier share D and gold (MAC04, MAC06); topics the news planner must cover when a flag turns; and the logged regime state (MAC10), an exploratory conditioning variable in REC03 and REC08. A MAC reading never sells, never sets a target and never skips a deposit.

families.name: Eligibility, product type, same-index grouping and data integrity (gates)
Implementation cost on the line
families.purpose: Line view (CST 50, TAX 24, DUR 19, EVT 7 = 100), ranked inside each same-index group across UCITS, US-listed and LSE ETP lines. Covers TER, tracking beyond TER, trading friction, traded value and order cost at deposit size by venue. CST10, at weight 0, is the single line-choice formula; when CST02 is missing it uses the fallback TERnow + TAX01 + entry cost for every group. Internal weights: CST01 0.30, CST02 0.35, CST04 0.15, CST06 0.15, CST08 0.05.

families.name: Withholding by wrapper, tax-rule fragility and distribution drag
Durability, custody and switch readiness
families.purpose: Line view: size, age and flows (DUR01, 0.6) and switch-ready substitutes (DUR06, 0.4). DUR02 is a gate on the custody and counterparty structure of gold ETCs, bitcoin products and ELN-based options-income funds, read from an owner etc_checks and btc_checks block in config. It is a record for swap lines and lending. Feeds the S1 and S2 sell rules.

families.name: Long-horizon expected return and valuation
families.purpose: Exposure view X (EXR 20, FAC 40, RSK 40 = 100; world reference = 50). Scored once per equity same-index group on its reference index. Only currency valuation (EXR06, 0.4, unverified and not built until a BIS probe passes) and 5-year reversal (EXR08, 0.6) are scored; while EXR06 is missing the family renormalises by coverage. EXR02 turns the scored pillars into a beta-consistent expected excess return for FIT04, with unestimated priors labelled. Valuation composites, bond and gold valuation are context. The value cluster (EXR06 + EXR08 + FAC01) is capped at 25% of X. Weights are unchanged from v2.

families.name: Rewarded factor exposure
families.purpose: Exposure view. Value, profitability, orthogonalised investment and quality-conditioned size loadings come from one common set (Ken French Developed 5 factors plus momentum), shrunk by their t-statistics and scored relative to the world. Internal weights: FAC01 0.12, FAC02 0.30, FAC03 0.28, FAC04 0.30. FAC05 holds the system's single beta, which OPT01 and OPT03 also use. FAC06 is the momentum record, tested only as one pre-registered REC04 variant.

families.name: Holdability and portfolio risk limits
families.purpose: Exposure view, one-sided against the world. Covers the excess drawdown path (RSK01, 0.35), downside asymmetry (RSK03, 0.35) and tail fatness (RSK05, 0.30). Being calmer than the world earns nothing above 50. RSK06 (drawdown budget) and RSK07 (risk-contribution ratio) are portfolio constraints at weight 0, including the bitcoin and options-income sleeves.

families.name: Look-through exposure hazards
families.purpose: Not in X. CON02 is the look-through composition context; the portfolio limits sit in FIT07 and FIT08. CON04 (restricted markets, unverified until config/restricted_markets.csv exists) and CON05 (thematic hype) are line gates. Spot bitcoin is governed by FIT13 instead of CON05.

families.name: Options-income scoring (O view)
Speculative bitcoin sleeve
families.purpose: Display and constraint input only. Bitcoin has no cash flows and no factor model that X could use. BTC01 leads with the stress replay and the US$ loss at the 5% cap, then shows volatility, drawdown, correlation and the risk share, labelled speculative in every table. It feeds FIT13, RSK06, RSK07 and the owner note. Line choice inside the bitcoin group uses the line view.

families.name: Fit with the owner's mix and portfolio limits
families.purpose:
Fit view (FIT = 100; current portfolio = 50, or the owner mix at target until positions exist).
- Equity groups: FIT04 0.40, FIT05 0.20, FIT06 0.20, FIT10 0.20.
- Gold, bonds, bitcoin and options-income: FIT05, FIT06 and FIT10 at 1/3 each.
Routing input and hard constraints at weight 0: sleeve gap (FIT01, a zero start allowed when positions_as_of is set), look-through US and sector limits against the owner's mix, line count and same-index guard, the US$60,000 US-situs cap (FIT12) and the 5% bitcoin cap and options-income limit (FIT13). FIT12 and FIT13 always bind and fail closed for buying until their config inputs exist.

families.name: Live record and rule testing

pillars.name: Global macro and central banks
pillars.definition: Lead agent plus explorer rounds (news_agent_design). Scope: Fed, ECB, BoE, BoJ, PBoC, SNB and CBUAE decisions, guidance and minutes, plus growth, labour and inflation surprises published in the ISO-week window. Scores global_equity, us_large_broad, developed_ex_us, em_broad, govt_bonds and gold_precious from -2 to +2 for the next 1-3 months, each against the world, with confidence and at least 2 dated sources. Also gives an absolute risk-on, neutral or risk-off label, logged only and never used to time deposits (S0). A score of +/-2 needs the policy decision or official release itself as a source. The planner must cover this pillar when MAC01, MAC04 or MAC08 turns its flag.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: federalreserve.gov, ecb.europa.eu, bankofengland.co.uk, boj.or.jp, pbc.gov.cn, snb.ch, centralbank.ae, BLS, BEA, Eurostat. Tier 2: Reuters, Bloomberg, FT, WSJ. The week pack carries the MAC01-MAC10 readings.
pillars.better_when: higher (+2 = strong tailwind for the group against the world); display and record only
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1. Scheduled macro announcements carry much of the equity premium (Savor and Wilson 2013), but their direction has no known out-of-sample timing value (Welch and Goyal 2008). The score is logged for REC08 and moves no money until it passes.
pillars.applies_to: UCITS, US-listed, options-income (via underlying), bitcoin (absolute risk note only); per fund group, same-index lines once

pillars.name: Rates, inflation and credit
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on Treasury, Bund, gilt and JGB yields and auctions, the term premium, inflation prints and expectations, investment-grade and high-yield spreads, defaults, private-credit and bank-funding stress, and sovereign rating actions. Scores govt_bonds, credit_bonds, financials, utilities_realestate and tech_ai_semis (long-duration growth) from -2 to +2 against the world. Structural facts about bond funds go to EVT01 and EVT02. The planner must cover this pillar when MAC02 or MAC04 turns its flag.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: US Treasury and debt-office auction results, rating-agency releases, central-bank financial stability reports. Tier 2 press. Context from MAC02 and MAC04.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (rates and credit). The excess bond premium carries information on future activity (Gilchrist and Zakrajsek 2012), but it has no tested timing value for a monthly depositor, so the score is recorded only.

pillars.name: US equities and earnings
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on the US earnings season (beat rate, guidance and estimate revisions), margins, buybacks, breadth, small and mid caps, value against growth, and US regulation affecting profits. Trade and fiscal policy belongs to NWS17. Scores us_large_broad (the S&P 500 group), us_small_mid_value, us_factor_dividend and consumer from -2 to +2 against the world. It also scores the S&P 500 options-income group against its underlying. Each earnings fact must cite the company release, an SEC 10-Q or 8-K, or a tier-2 report of it.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: SEC EDGAR filings and company releases, S&P DJI. Tier 2: Reuters, Bloomberg, WSJ.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1. The S&P 500 is 19% of the owner's mix after the bitcoin change. Index-level earnings surprises relate weakly, or even negatively, to later index returns (Kothari, Lewellen and Warner 2006), so the score's sign must earn its vote in REC08.

pillars.name: Technology, AI and semiconductors
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on hyperscaler capital spending, AI demand and pricing, the chip supply chain (TSMC, Nvidia, ASML, memory makers), chip export controls, antitrust actions, power and data-centre limits, and results from the largest Nasdaq-100 companies. Scores tech_ai_semis (the Nasdaq-100 group), us_large_broad, global_equity and em_asia_other (Taiwan, Korea) from -2 to +2 against the world. It also scores the Nasdaq-100 options-income groups against their underlying. A rise in mega-cap concentration is flagged to EVT04 and FIT08.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: company releases and filings, US Commerce Department export rules (BIS), MOFCOM, index-provider notices. Tier 2 press. iShares holdings CSV for weights.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1. In the owner's mix, US look-through is 69.4% against 59.9% for the world (REPORT_V2 FIT07), and IT plus Communication Services set the FIT08 sector limit. Theme-attention cycles end in underperformance (Ben-David, Franzoni, Kim and Moussawi 2023).

pillars.name: Cyclical sectors and financials
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on banks and insurers (results, capital rules, stress tests), industrials and defence (orders, procurement budgets), materials and mining equities, transport, and consumer discretionary and housing. Scores financials, industrials_defense_infra, materials_mining_metals and consumer from -2 to +2 against the world.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: company releases; regulators (Fed stress tests, EBA, Basel Committee); defence budget documents. Tier 2 press. yfinance returns for each sector group.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (other sectors). Industry momentum exists before costs (Moskowitz and Grinblatt 1999), but sector rotation lost to holding here (backtest_latest S1/S2). The score is recorded only, and CON05 and FIT08 limit sector lines.

pillars.name: Defensive sectors and real assets
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on healthcare and biotech (drug pricing, FDA and EMA decisions, patent expiries), consumer staples, utilities and power demand, REITs and infrastructure, telecoms, and clean-energy policy. Scores healthcare_biotech, utilities_realestate, consumer (staples) and clean_energy_thematic from -2 to +2 against the world.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: FDA, EMA, CMS, utility regulators, company releases. Tier 2 press.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (other sectors). Staples, utilities and property groups top X this week (XDWS, IUCS and GLRA at 74 in REPORT_V2), so their news is needed to read those scores. Splitting sectors into two pillars keeps each agent's scope small enough to saturate.

pillars.name: Europe, UK and other developed markets
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on euro-area and UK growth and inflation data, transmission of ECB and BoE policy, national fiscal and defence spending, energy prices, elections and coalitions, Switzerland, the Nordics and Canada. Scores europe and developed_ex_us from -2 to +2 against the world.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: Eurostat, ONS, ECB, BoE, the European Commission, national finance ministries. Tier 2 press.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (Europe). Developed ex-US is the leading X candidate (EXUS smoothed X 65.0 in REC04), so its news must be logged point-in-time now for a later test to be possible.

pillars.name: Japan and developed Asia-Pacific
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on BoJ policy, JGB yields and the yen (including carry-trade positioning), wage talks, Tokyo Stock Exchange governance reform and buybacks, Japanese earnings, and Australia, Singapore and Hong Kong. Scores japan, asia_dev_other and developed_ex_us from -2 to +2 against the world. Carry-unwind risk is flagged for global_equity and MAC03.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: boj.or.jp, JPX/TSE, MoF Japan, RBA. Tier 2: Nikkei Asia, Reuters, Bloomberg. yfinance JPY=X.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (Japan). Japan is the largest non-US weight in VWRA. The August 2024 yen carry unwind took the Nikkei 225 down 12.4% on 5 August 2024.

pillars.name: China and Hong Kong
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on Chinese activity data, PBoC and fiscal stimulus, the property sector, regulation of tech platforms, US-China relations (entity lists, outbound investment rules), and ADR delisting and VIE risk. Scores china, em_broad and em_asia_other from -2 to +2 against the world. Facts on sanctions, capital controls or delisting go to EVT07 for gate treatment.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: NBS, PBoC, CSRC, MOFCOM, US Treasury (OFAC and outbound investment), HKEX notices. Tier 2 press.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (China). China is the largest weight in EM indices and the main source of CON04 restricted-market risk. Russia's 2022 removal from indices at near-zero prices shows that part of the risk is structural, and that part is handled by EVT07.

pillars.name: India
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on RBI policy and the rupee, Indian earnings and valuations, foreign portfolio flows, elections and reforms, index-weight changes, and Indian tax on foreign portfolio investors. That tax is paid inside UCITS India funds and lowers their NAV, so changes also go to EVT06 and TAX01. Scores india and em_broad from -2 to +2 against the world.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: rbi.org.in, SEBI, Indian budget and CBDT notices, NSDL foreign-investor flow data. Tier 2 press.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (India). India's July 2024 budget raised capital-gains tax on foreign portfolio investors (long-term from 10% to 12.5%, short-term from 15% to 20%), a structural drag on India funds' NAV.

pillars.name: Other emerging markets
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on Taiwan, Korea (the value-up programme), ASEAN, Brazil, Mexico, South Africa and Turkey; EM currencies and EM debt; and the MSCI and FTSE market-classification reviews (reclassifications go to EVT04). Scores em_asia_other, latam and em_broad from -2 to +2 against the world.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: national central banks and statistics offices, MSCI and FTSE Russell classification reviews. Tier 2 press. FRED DTWEXBGS.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (other emerging markets). A stronger dollar tightens EM financial conditions (Avdjiev, Bruno, Koch and Shin 2019), which is why this pillar reads MAC05. EIMI has an X of 48.8 in REC04, close to neutral.

pillars.name: Gulf, Middle East and geopolitics
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on Saudi, UAE and Qatar markets and budgets, oil-linked fiscal positions, MSCI and FTSE index events in the Gulf, wars and ceasefires, shipping through Hormuz and the Red Sea, Russia-Ukraine, the Taiwan Strait, and elections. Scores mena_gulf, energy_oil, gold_precious and global_equity (absolute, logged only) from -2 to +2. Also writes an owner safety note on the AED peg, UAE banks and remittances, which goes to EVT08. Formal sanctions go to EVT07.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: CBUAE, SAMA, Tadawul, ADX and DFM notices, OFAC, EU and UK statements, UKMTO shipping notices. Tier 2: Reuters, Bloomberg, The National. The Caldara-Iacoviello GPR page.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (Gulf and geopolitics). Geopolitical shocks lower equity returns on impact, with mostly transitory effects (Caldara and Iacoviello 2022). The owner lives in the UAE and funds deposits in AED. Oil rose 28.9% in the 3 months to 2026-11-03.
pillars.applies_to: UCITS, US-listed, bitcoin (risk note) (per fund group)

pillars.name: Commodities and energy
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on OPEC+ decisions, oil and gas inventories and supply outages, central-bank gold buying, silver, copper, battery metals, uranium, agriculture and broad commodity indices. Each oil move must be classified as supply-driven or demand-driven. Scores energy_oil, materials_mining_metals, gold_precious and commodities_broad from -2 to +2 against the world. The planner must cover this pillar when MAC07 turns its flag.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: OPEC, IEA, EIA weekly reports, World Gold Council, LBMA. Tier 2 press. FRED DCOILBRENTEU; yfinance CL=F, GC=F, HG=F.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (commodities and energy). Oil supply shocks and demand shocks move equities in opposite directions (Kilian and Park 2009), so the agent must name which kind it is. Gold is an owner-sized sleeve candidate (IGLN).

pillars.name: Fund flows and positioning
pillars.definition:
Explorer rounds on ETF and mutual-fund flows by group (ICI, issuer and exchange flow reports), CFTC positioning, fund-manager and AAII surveys, margin debt, short interest, spot bitcoin ETF flows, and the assets and launches of leveraged, single-stock and other information-only ETFs, read here as a gauge of froth. The sign rule is pre-registered as contrarian at extremes. A group gets -1 or -2 only when a cited series is at a historical extreme (top 5% for inflows, bullishness or crowding), and +1 for capitulation outflows; otherwise it scores 0.
Two parts:
- agent part: web search, verified, runs now;
- code part: group share-count flows from the REC02 snapshot store, which does not exist yet. Until it has 52 weekly snapshots, NWS14 scores from the agent part only and is logged with the flag partial.
pillars.data_source: Web search: ICI, CFTC Commitments of Traders, AAII, FINRA margin statistics, issuer flow pages (verified). Code: yfinance and iShares shares outstanding through the REC02 snapshot store (not yet created).
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (flows and positioning). Retail flows are followed by lower returns (Frazzini and Lamont 2008), and aggregate equity-fund flows partly reverse (Ben-Rephael, Kandel and Wohl 2012). Contrarian use is unproven, so the score is record only. Labelled unverified because its code part depends on a store that does not exist yet (audit round 1).
pillars.applies_to: UCITS, US-listed, bitcoin, options-income (per fund group)

pillars.name: Crypto and bitcoin ETF news
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: SEC and CFTC releases, sponsor notices and S-1 or 10-K filings on EDGAR, custodian notices, fca.org.uk, vara.ae. Tier 2: Reuters, Bloomberg; CoinDesk labelled tier 2. yfinance BTC-USD and spot ETF prices.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirements 1 and 4. Crypto returns are driven by crypto-specific momentum and attention, not by equity factors (Liu and Tsyvinski 2021). US spot ETFs began trading on 2024-01-11.

pillars.name: Options-income fund news
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: issuer notices, 19a-1 and N-CSR/N-PORT filings on EDGAR, UCITS KIDs and issuer pages (JPMorgan AM, Global X), Cboe. Tier 2 press. Context from MAC03 and OPT04.
pillars.better_when: higher (better for the group against its underlying); display and record only
pillars.evidence: Owner requirements 1 and 4. A covered call is long equity, short volatility and short a dynamic equity position (Israelov and Nielsen 2015). A distribution cut is not by itself a loss of value.

pillars.name: Trade, tariffs and fiscal policy
pillars.definition: Explorer rounds on US tariffs and court rulings, retaliation, export controls beyond chips, deficits, debt-limit and shutdown events, and any proposal to tax foreign holders of US assets (for example a retaliatory withholding surcharge). Such proposals go to EVT06 at once, because they would change TAX01 and FIT12. Scores every affected group from -2 to +2 against the world, especially us_large_broad, tech_ai_semis, china, europe and em_broad.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: USTR, the Federal Register, Congress.gov, court dockets, Treasury. Tier 2 press.
pillars.evidence: Tariff announcements in 2018-2019 and April 2025 caused sharp one-week index moves that later largely reversed. The 2025 proposal for a surcharge on investors from 'discriminatory' countries (section 899) was dropped before enactment, but it showed that rules can target foreign holders, and for a UAE resident holding US-listed lines such measures are structural.

pillars.name: Fund corporate actions
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: issuer notices, investegate.co.uk RNS (daily NAV notices filtered out), SEC EDGAR 497, N-14, N-8F and 8-K filings, and ETP issuer notices.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 5: structural events act at once. Owner requirement 1: every news pillar is scored per group on -2..+2, so the group score is added and severity stays the gate. A closure forces a switch whatever the scores say, and closures cluster in small, young funds (DUR01).

pillars.name: Fees, structure, strategy and cheaper substitutes
pillars.definition:
The agent detects and cites changes to:
- TER or sponsor fee, including the end of a bitcoin fee waiver;
- replication, securities lending, distribution policy, domicile and KID availability;
- options-income strategy (overwrite ratio, strike rule, ELN or listed options, payout frequency).
It also finds new same-index lines, such as a UCITS twin of a US-only product.
It seeds missing TERs from issuer KIDs: IB1T.L, BTCW.L, QYLD.L, QYLU.L and any other line with a blank ter column. This is required before the first order in their groups, and each probe is logged in CHANGELOG. Confirmed TER changes are appended to ter_history (CST01).
Output 1, line severity: an adverse confirmed change is 2. The cheaper-substitute trigger is computed by code: severity 1 when an eligible same-index substitute's CST10 is 10 bps or more lower, after US withholding and FIT12 headroom.
Output 2, group score from -2 to +2: adverse severity 1/2/3 gives -1/-2/-2 for the group. A confirmed fee cut, a cheaper same-index substitute or a new UCITS twin gives +1. Penalty-only in the line view.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: issuer KIDs, prospectus supplements and notices, SEC 485 and 497 filings, justETF profiles (agent part verified by data test 1: iShares KID parsed, EDGAR J.P. Morgan ETF Trust filings listed, justETF profiles parsed). The code substitute trigger reads CST10 from v2_line_values.csv: verified for UCITS lines, unverified for US lines until those rows are added.
pillars.better_when: severity 0; a cheaper substitute becomes an S2 candidate
pillars.evidence: S2 cost switches need confirmed fee and structure facts. VWRA's fee cut to 0.14% (effective 2026-07-28) changed line costs mid-year. Round 2 change: only the US-line code trigger is unverified, so the agent part is not zero-weighted as a whole (execution audit).

pillars.name: Index methodology, reclassification and mega-cap events
pillars.definition:
The agent tracks benchmark switches, provider consultations, capping-rule changes, special rebalances, country reclassifications, changes to the reference index of an options-income fund or to the bitcoin reference rate, and single-company events that move top-10 weights. It also keeps each line's benchmark-change history in the snapshot store.
Any confirmed change triggers an immediate recompute of ELG07 groups, FIT07, FIT08 and CON02 from fresh holdings. A change that takes a line out of its same-index group is severity 2 and opens S1.
Group score from -2 to +2:
- adverse severity 1/2/3 (for example a methodology change that raises concentration, or an index downgrade) gives -1/-2/-2 for the affected groups;
- a confirmed favourable change (for example a capping rule that lowers single-name concentration, or an upgrade into a broad index) gives +1.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: MSCI, FTSE Russell, S&P DJI, Nasdaq, Cboe and CF Benchmarks announcements, SEC EDGAR. Weekly snapshot of the benchmark field.
pillars.evidence: The Nasdaq-100 special rebalance of July 2023 cut mega-cap weights within a week. Issuers switch indices to cut licence fees, and a benchmark switch can move a line out of its sleeve. A group score was added for owner requirement 1.

pillars.name: Issuer, custodian and counterparty health
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: notices from the Central Bank of Ireland, CSSF, FCA, SEC, FINRA and Jersey FSC; issuer and custodian releases; rating-agency actions.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (issuer and custodian health). Custody failure is the main non-market loss channel for bitcoin (Mt Gox 2014, FTX 2022), and Coinbase Custody holds the coins of IBIT and most US spot ETFs (IBIT prospectus, data test 6). ELN-based premium-income funds add bank counterparties: JEPQ's N-PORT for 2026-06-30 shows about 16% of net assets in ELNs from 5 banks.

pillars.name: Tax and legal regime for a UAE resident
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: IRS (the nonresident estate-tax page fetched and confirms US$60,000, data test 5), Treasury, Federal Register, Revenue.ie, UAE MoF and FTA, CRA, OECD, the European Commission, FCA.
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (tax and legal for a UAE resident). The US$60,000 cap and the 30% and 15% withholding rates are the inputs to TAX01, CST10 and FIT12, and Branch A of plan v5 rests on these rules.

pillars.name: Sanctions, capital controls and market access (gate)
pillars.definition:
The agent detects sanctions, capital controls, exchange closures, investment bans and delisting risk that affect look-through holdings or the owner's ability to transact. It estimates the affected weight per line and proposes rows for config/restricted_markets.csv, each with a primary-source URL and the quoted text. Code checks each row before CON04 uses it. Severity 3 blocks deposits to the affected lines at once. Weight 0 in X.
Group score from -2 to +2: severity 1/2/3 gives -1/-2/-2 for groups whose look-through weight in the affected market is 2% or more (for example china, em_broad). The lifting of a measure, confirmed by a primary source, gives +1.
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: OFAC, EU, UK OFSI and UAE sanctions lists; index-provider and exchange notices.
pillars.evidence: Russian holdings were frozen and written down after the 2022 index removals. A group score was added for owner requirement 1.

pillars.name: Broker, venue, product access and funding channel
pillars.data_source: Web search. Primary sources: IBKR pricing pages and notices; LSE, NYSE and Nasdaq notices; CBUAE releases. IBKR account facts themselves come only from the owner (ELG08).
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 1 (broker and funding channel). Whether US-listed lines and LSE bitcoin ETNs can be bought at all depends on the IBKR entity, PRIIPs rules and the crypto permission. CST08 and CST10 depend on the US commission and fractional-share terms.

pillars.name: Deposit-week calendar and market dislocations
pillars.definition:
The agent lists the deposit-week events: FOMC, US CPI and payrolls, ECB, BoE and BoJ meetings, index rebalance days, option expiries, ex-dates of held distributing lines, and US, UK and UAE holidays. It adds any ETF dislocation, exchange outage, or bitcoin ETP gap after a large weekend move.
It recommends the order day and session (LSE 14:30-16:15 London; US 10:00-15:30 New York), given MAC03's state. It may delay an order by at most 1 week, and every delay is logged in REC05. It never skips a deposit or triggers a sale.
Per-group execution score on the -2..+2 scale, limited to -1 or 0: -1 when the group due an order this month has a conflict in its order window, otherwise 0. It is logged in news_log.csv but kept out of N and out of REC08's primary test, because it forecasts order-day friction, not 1-3 month returns. It is tested against realised entry cost in REC05.
pillars.data_source: Web search; central-bank, index-provider and exchange calendars; MAC03 readings.
pillars.better_when: no conflict in the order window (0)
pillars.evidence: Spreads widen around volatility spikes and major releases (Chordia, Roll and Subrahmanyam 2001). A delay of days costs little, while skipping a deposit costs the equity premium. Bitcoin trades all week but ETPs only in exchange hours. The group score meets requirement 1's scale, and the stated reason explains why it is kept out of N.

pillars.name: Recession indicators
pillars.data_source: FRED T10Y3M, T10Y2Y, SAHMREALTIME, RECPROUSM156N, one series per request via curl --http1.1, with cached fallback (verified 2026-11-13)
pillars.better_when: context only; flag off is calmer
pillars.evidence: The curve forecasts recessions (Estrella and Mishkin 1998), and the Sahm rule marks their early stage (Sahm 2019). Neither forecasts equity returns out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008), and trend-selling the core lost 0.6-1.8 points a year here.

pillars.name: Credit stress
pillars.data_source: FRED BAA10Y (from 1986), BAMLH0A0HYM2, BAMLC0A0CM, BAMLEMCBPIOAS (3-year window), one series per request via curl --http1.1; yfinance HYG, IEF
pillars.better_when: context only; lower spreads are calmer
pillars.evidence: Financial conditions predict the downside tail of growth (Adrian, Boyarchenko and Giannone 2019), but they have no tested timing value for a depositor. REPORT_V2: high-yield OAS 3.34%, up 0.64 in 3 months.

pillars.name: Volatility regime (execution caution and option premium)
pillars.definition: Readings: VIX, VIX/VIX3M, VXN and MOVE. When VIX is above 30, VIX/VIX3M above 1 or MOVE above 140, the execution ladder starts at mid and avoids the first and last 30 minutes of the LSE and US sessions. VIX and VXN levels also go to OPT04 and NWS16 as the premium environment for options-income. A deposit is never delayed beyond EVT09's one week and never skipped.
pillars.data_source: yfinance ^VIX, ^VIX3M, ^VXN, ^MOVE; FRED VIXCLS and VXNCLS as fallback (verified)
pillars.evidence: Spreads widen when volatility spikes (Petajisto 2017). W46: VIX 25.6 and VIX/VIX3M 1.04, so the caution state applied. Covered-call income rises with implied volatility.

pillars.name: Real rates, inflation and term premium
pillars.definition: Readings: the 10-year TIPS yield and its 3-month change; the 5-year breakeven and 5y5y forward; core CPI 3-month annualised against its 12-month rate; core PCE year on year; the Kim-Wright 10-year term premium (FRED THREEFYTP10, labelled as Kim-Wright, not ACM; the New York Fed ACM series is optional context once probed); and the 2-year yield. Pre-registered flag: on if core CPI 3-month annualised is above 4% and above its 12-month rate, or the TIPS yield rose 50 bps or more in 3 months. Context for the owner's diversifier share D, for long-duration growth sleeves, and for NWS01 and NWS02.
pillars.data_source: FRED DFII10, T5YIE, T5YIFR, CPILFESL, PCEPILFE, THREEFYTP10 (Kim-Wright), DGS2, one series per request via curl --http1.1 (verified)
pillars.evidence: Rising real yields hit long-duration equity hardest: the Nasdaq-100 fell 6.7 points beyond its beta in 2022 (REPORT_V2 RSK04). The inflation regime governs whether bonds hedge equities (Ilmanen 2003). The term-premium label was corrected in round 2 (data audit).

pillars.name: Dollar and AED peg
pillars.data_source: FRED DTWEXBGS; yfinance AED=X, EURUSD=X, JPY=X, GBPUSD=X, CNY=X (replaces CNH=X, which returned 0 rows over 1 year; CNY=X returned 260 rows), INR=X (verified); FRED DEXCHUS as CNY fallback (unverified until probed)
pillars.evidence: Deposits arrive in AED, so a peg break is the one macro event that would change the owner's USD cash directly. Dollar strength tightens EM conditions (Avdjiev et al. 2019). REPORT_V2: broad dollar +2.4% in 3 months.

pillars.name: Stock-bond correlation and diversifier regime
pillars.definition: Readings: the 36-month correlation of monthly world-reference returns (VWRA spliced with VT) with IEF total returns, and its 20-year percentile; whether Treasuries rose in each of the last 3 world drawdowns of 10% or more; the same correlation for gold. Pre-registered flag: on if the stock-bond correlation is above +0.3, meaning bonds are not hedging. Context for the owner's D (0-20%) and gold (0 or 5%) decisions, for FIT05 and for the RSK06 replay. It never sets a target.
pillars.data_source: yfinance VT, IEF, GC=F, VWRA.L with the ELG07 world splice (verified)
pillars.better_when: context only; negative correlation means bonds diversify
pillars.evidence: The stock-bond correlation turns positive in high-inflation regimes (Ilmanen 2003), as in 2022. That is why the bond sleeve is owner-sized, not score-targeted.

pillars.name: Oil, commodity and growth shock
pillars.definition: Readings: Brent and WTI 3-month change and 10-year percentile; the 6-month change in the copper/gold ratio as a growth gauge; the 6-month annualised change in US industrial production. Pre-registered flag: on if Brent moved 30% or more either way in 3 months, or copper/gold fell 15% or more in 6 months. When the flag is on, NWS12 and NWS13 must cover it and must classify the shock as supply or demand.
pillars.data_source: FRED DCOILBRENTEU, DCOILWTICO, INDPRO; yfinance CL=F, HG=F, GC=F (verified 2026-11-13)
pillars.evidence: Oil price spikes preceded most US recessions (Hamilton 1983), but supply and demand shocks affect equities differently (Kilian and Park 2009). Oil rose 28.9% in the 3 months to 2026-11-03.

pillars.name: Financial conditions and liquidity
pillars.definition: Readings: Chicago Fed NFCI and ANFCI, level and 13-week change; the St. Louis Fed stress index; Fed net liquidity (WALCL - WTREGEN - RRPONTSYD, units aligned to US$ billions) and its 13-week change; real M2 growth over 12 months. Pre-registered flag: on if NFCI is above 0, the stress index is above 1, or net liquidity fell US$250bn or more in 13 weeks. Net liquidity is labelled 'popular, unproven' in every output. Context for the drawdown note, NWS01 and bitcoin.
pillars.data_source: FRED NFCI, ANFCI, STLFSI4, WALCL, WTREGEN, RRPONTSYD, M2SL, CPIAUCSL, one series per request via curl --http1.1 with cached fallback (verified)
pillars.evidence: Liquidity shocks precede forced selling (Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009). Net liquidity has no peer-reviewed evidence on returns, so it is context and test material only.

pillars.name: Market drawdown, trend and breadth state (guardrails)
pillars.data_source: yfinance VWRA.L spliced with VT; RSP, SPY; iShares IVV holdings (verified)
pillars.evidence: Selling the core on its own downtrend (backtest S8) returned 10.02% against 11.85% for holding. Momentum crashes cluster in rebounds after bear markets (Daniel and Moskowitz 2016). Investors lose 1-1.7 points a year by trading around drawdowns (Dichev 2007).

pillars.name: Regime state and risk-off count (record)
pillars.definition: Counts the pre-registered flags from MAC01, MAC02 and MAC04-MAC09 (0 to 8; MAC03 is excluded as an execution state), plus a policy-uncertainty flag when daily US EPU is above its 5-year 90th percentile. State: calm (0-1), watch (2-3), stress (4 or more). Also derives a growth-inflation quadrant. Logged weekly in REC02 with the config hash and used as a prior by the news planner. In REC03 and REC08 it is an exploratory conditioning variable, never part of the gating test. It never moves money.
pillars.data_source: MAC01-MAC09 outputs; FRED USEPUINDXD (verified); Caldara-Iacoviello GPR (logged when available)
pillars.evidence: Composites of predictors do little better out of sample (Welch and Goyal 2008; Campbell and Thompson 2008). Pre-registering the count now makes an honest live test possible later. Owner requirement 2 (macro regime, computed).

pillars.name: Wrapper, domicile and US-situs class (gate)
pillars.definition:
Assigns each line one class:
(a) IE or LU UCITS, not US-situs. Eligible for any sleeve; IE is preferred over LU on the same index.
(b) IE- or Jersey-issued physically backed precious-metal ETC. Gold sleeve only; needs DUR02.
(c) US-domiciled 1940-Act ETF listed on NYSE Arca, Nasdaq or Cboe. A US-listed candidate: US-situs, counted in FIT12, 30% investor withholding (TAX01), 10 bps CST10 hurdle.
(d) US spot bitcoin grantor trust. Bitcoin sleeve only; US-situs, counted in FIT12; needs DUR02.
(e) Physically backed bitcoin ETP issued outside the US and listed on the LSE (BTCW.L, IB1T.L and peers). Bitcoin sleeve only. These are secured notes (ETNs) backed by bitcoin held by a custodian, with a security trustee. They are not ETFs and not US-situs. They need DUR02, the owner's IBKR crypto-ETP permission (ELG08), and a TER seeded from the KID (EVT02). If none is orderable for the owner's IBKR entity, the bitcoin sleeve falls to class (d) inside FIT12 headroom.
Everything else fails: US partnerships and K-1 commodity pools (10% gross-proceeds withholding under IRC 1446(f)), unsecured or synthetic ETNs and crypto notes, closed-end funds, US mutual funds and non-UCITS European funds. A held line moving to fail triggers S1.
pillars.data_source: universe_ucits_*.csv, config/universe_us_core.csv and config/universe_us_new_types.csv (ISIN, type; LSE bitcoin rows typed bitcoin_etn_lse); yfinance quoteType, legalType and fundFamily (verified for US funds); SEC EDGAR registration type; issuer prospectus, S-1 or base prospectus
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 3. Shares of US corporations are US-situs for estate tax (IRC 2104); Irish funds are not. With no US-UAE treaty, US distributions to a non-resident alien carry 30% (IRC 871(a), 1441), while the Ireland-US treaty gives Irish funds 15%. Class (e) widens the owner's 'spot bitcoin ETFs' to physically backed LSE notes, because they carry the same exposure without US estate exposure. Their ETN form and access condition are now stated (execution audit).

pillars.name: Quote currency, venue and price-unit check (gate)
pillars.definition: Passes a line that trades in USD on the LSE or on a US primary exchange. GBp, GBP and EUR LSE lines are mapped to their USD sibling by ISIN (for example JEGP.L to JEPG.L, JEIP.L to JEPI.L, QYLP.L to QYLD.L, SPXP.L to SPXS.L). A non-USD line (for example IB1T.L in GBP) is eligible only if its group has no affordable eligible USD line, and its FX cost is then charged in CST10. Flags 100x GBp/GBP unit jumps.
pillars.data_source: yfinance currency and exchange fields; universe ISINs
pillars.evidence: Deposits are converted to USD once (US$2 minimum), so a second conversion is pure cost. v2 found fake gaps of 292-342 bps from comparing GBp with USD. Probed on 2026-11-13: JEPG.L, JEPQ.L and BTCW.L quote in USD; IB1T.L quotes in GBP.

pillars.name: Product type and information-only gate
pillars.data_source: config/universe_us_new_types.csv (15 leveraged_info rows; single_stock column; index column for BTCI, SVOL, ULTY, YMAX); yfinance category (for example 'Trading--Leveraged Equity', 'Derivative Income', 'Digital Assets'); prospectus via EDGAR or KID
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 4. Daily-reset leverage decays with volatility (Cheng and Madhavan 2009). Futures roll costs make futures-based bitcoin funds track spot poorly, and single-stock risk is not rewarded. Round 2 adds BTCI, which would otherwise hold bitcoin outside the 5% cap, and SVOL, YMAX and ULTY, which are volatility-futures or single-stock option products (owner audit). That leaves 145 US-listed buy candidates.

pillars.name: Asset class and sleeve mapping (gate)
pillars.definition: Maps each line to one sleeve: world, S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, an equity satellite (region, country, factor, sector), gold, diversifier bonds (investment-grade government or aggregate, duration 5 years or more), bitcoin (speculative), or options-income (tagged with its ELG07 underlying-and-strategy group). Money-market, T-bill, 0-1 year, ultra-short and multi-asset funds always fail; in the US universe this includes BIL, SGOV and SHY. Gold, bonds, bitcoin and options-income are owner-sized and never score-targeted. Lines with no pre-registered sleeve are scored but cannot receive deposits.
pillars.data_source: Universe type and scope columns; yfinance category; issuer asset-class and duration fields
pillars.evidence: In the v2 audit, the old composite correlated -0.77 with volatility and put 7 T-bill or bond funds in its top 20. Owner requirement 4 adds the bitcoin and options-income sleeves.

pillars.name: Feed freshness and price integrity
pillars.definition:
- Freshness: trading days since the last print with volume above 0 on the line's own exchange. More than 5 days: not buyable. More than 7 on a held line: an S1 review, confirmed by an issuer notice.
- Integrity: over 252 sessions, counts daily returns beyond 6 robust sigmas that the group reference does not match on the same or next day (same sign, at least half the size), plus unit jumps and runs of repeated closes. Bitcoin lines are checked against BTC-USD.
Any unmatched event suspends the line's price-based pillars until it is explained.
pillars.data_source: yfinance daily close and volume for .L and US lines; BTC-USD (verified)
pillars.evidence: Stale or broken prices corrupt every other pillar. CNDX.L printed the same close on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06. Two share classes of one fund (JEPG.L and JEGA.L) correlate only 0.89 on weekly LSE closes, which shows how noisy LSE feeds are.

pillars.name: Same-index groups across wrappers, proxy mapping and splice fidelity
pillars.data_source: Issuer benchmark fields; config/approved_equivalents.csv (to create); universe index column; yfinance monthly closes, ^NDX; cdn.cboe.com BXM_History.csv and BXN_History.csv fetched with redirects followed (curl -L; without it HTTP 307) (verified 2026-11-13)

pillars.name: IBKR orderability, permissions and W-8BEN (owner-confirmed)
pillars.definition:
The orderable block in config/portfolio_v2.yaml moves from a list to a dict:
orderable: {LINE: {ok, checked_on, ibkr_entity, venue, product_class, permission_needed, fractional_ok}}
Top-level fields are added: ibkr_entity, w8ben_signed_on and us_commission_plan.
Each entry is renewed every 100 days and whenever a line first enters a shortlist; if absent or expired, the line fails.
- US-listed lines also need confirmed US-ETF access for the owner's IBKR entity (no KID block) and a valid W-8BEN, signed within 3 calendar years (EVT08 warns 90 days before expiry).
- Bitcoin products need the crypto-ETP permission.
- Options-income lines need any complex-product acknowledgement.
VWRA is exempt. Entries the owner should check in TWS before any order: BTCW.L, IB1T.L, IBIT, JEPI.L, JEPQ.L, JEQA.L, JEGA.L and QYLU.L.
pillars.data_source: Owner check in TWS or the client portal, stored in config/portfolio_v2.yaml (orderable is [VWRA.L] today; dict schema and entity, venue and W-8BEN fields still to add)
pillars.evidence: REPORT_V2 marks every line except VWRA as not confirmed in IBKR. A W-8BEN stays valid until the end of the third calendar year after signing (Treas. Reg. 1.1441-1(e)(4)(ii)). The owner's 'bitcoin in at 5%' cannot execute until a bitcoin line is confirmed here (execution and data audits).

pillars.name: Data coverage, source freshness and cross-source reconciliation
pillars.definition:
- Coverage: the share of the line's scored pillar weight, counting verified sources only, that has a live reading this week. Below 70% the line cannot receive money (VWRA exempt).
- Age limits: holdings 35 days (45 for month-end publishers), tracking 100 days, TER 120 days, cached FRED and Shiller values 45 days. A blank TER (today IB1T.L, BTCW.L, QYLD.L and QYLU.L) blocks the line until EVT02 seeds it from the KID.
- Reconciliation across issuer, yfinance and justETF or SEC filings: TER within 2 bps, date-matched NAV within 20 bps, AUM within 10% (only below US$5bn), and holdings stand-ins within 2 points on region weights.
A breach blocks the affected pillar.
pillars.data_source: Engine pillar table; iShares pages and holdings CSV (blackrock.com/uk ajax CSV); Vanguard region table; justETF; yfinance info for .L and US funds; SEC N-PORT
pillars.evidence: Fund size is missing from Yahoo for 126 lines (REPORT_V2). The v2 audit found that filling missing values with 50 hid 14-23% gaps. Blank TERs were found on the LSE bitcoin and Global X lines in round 1 (quant audit).

pillars.name: TER or sponsor fee
pillars.definition: Ongoing charge of the exact share class, in bps a year: the UCITS TER, a US ETF's net expense ratio, or a bitcoin sponsor fee after any temporary waiver ends. Scored against the median eligible line in the same-index group with k = 10 bps; a single-line group uses an absolute anchor of 10 bps. Every change is appended to ter_history with date and source URL. Any rise opens EVT02 and S2. Blank TERs in the universe file are seeded from issuer KIDs by EVT02 before the line can be bought. Weight 0.30 of CST.
pillars.data_source: Issuer pages, justETF, KIDs (iShares KID parse verified); yfinance netExpenseRatio for US funds (verified: VOO 0.03, QQQM 0.15, JEPI 0.35, IBIT 0.25); universe ter column (blank for IB1T.L, BTCW.L, QYLD.L, QYLU.L until seeded); S-1 fee schedules
pillars.evidence: Fees are the one certain drag (Sharpe 1991) and the best predictor of fund outcomes (Morningstar fee studies).

pillars.name: Tracking beyond TER and its stability
pillars.definition:
G_i is the annualised gap between the line's USD total return and the group reference line's, over at least 3 years (5 where available), using 20-day average prices at both ends and restated at current TERs. CST02_i = G_i + (TERnow_i - TERnow_ref), shrunk toward 0 by a standard error estimated from the spread of the last 5 calendar-year gaps.
Measurement bases:
- US-listed lines: price plus distributions before investor withholding, which TAX01 charges, so it is counted once;
- bitcoin lines: against BTC-USD at the fund's fixing time.
Not applied to options-income lines, which OPT03 scores. Missing for the whole group until ter_history covers every line in it; CST10 then uses its fallback. Weight 0.35 of CST.
pillars.data_source: yfinance daily closes and dividends; ter_history from annual reports (iShares VII annual report parses); iShares calendar-year tracking tables (parse for 2016-2025)
pillars.evidence: Tracking difference persists by fund (Elton, Gruber, Comer and Li 2002) and captures withholding, lending and swap effects that TER misses. Measured on 2026-11-07: SPXS +19.3 bps against CSPX. Only a raw gap exists today (CST02_raw_gap_bps), so the pillar is unverified until ter_history is seeded.

pillars.name: Trading friction: spread, NAV premium and price noise
pillars.data_source: yfinance closes, bid, ask, regularMarketTime; iShares Historical NAVs sheet; US issuer NAV pages
pillars.evidence: Round-trip friction is paid on every deposit and switch. v2 data test 2 found crossed or stale Yahoo LSE quotes (a CSPX bid above the ask). IBIT's spread was about 5 bps on 2026-11-13. The noise part is verified; the spread and premium parts are not yet.

pillars.name: Traded value and zero-volume days
pillars.definition: Log of the 63-session median daily traded value on the traded line (close x volume, in US$), saturating at US$5m a day, minus a penalty for the share of zero-volume sessions (none at 0%, maximum at 20% or more). Also sets the switch-size rule for S1, S2, S7 and S8: split across sessions above 10% of median daily traded value. Most US lines saturate. Weight 0.15 of CST.
pillars.data_source: yfinance daily volume and close (verified)
pillars.evidence: Thin LSE lines (FWRA about US$3.6m a day) need split switches. Its redundancy with DUR01 is tested in REC03.

pillars.name: Order cost at deposit size: commission, residue and fractions
pillars.definition:
For orders of US$340-760:
- the commission as a share of the order, by venue: LSE US$1.70 minimum; US-listed at the owner's IBKR plan, assumed US$1.00 minimum until EVT08 or the owner's us_commission_plan confirms it;
- plus the expected whole-share residue: (order - commission - floor((order - commission) / price) x price) / order.
Residue is 0 where ELG08 confirms fractional shares for that venue. A line priced above 0.9 x US$679 is flagged as not buyable in one month. US$340 is the system-wide minimum order, including bitcoin orders and split remainders, so the US$1.70 commission stays at or below 0.5%. Weight 0.05 of CST; its money cost is priced in CST10.
pillars.data_source: yfinance USD prices; commission constants in config/portfolio_v2.yaml (LSE commission_min_usd 1.70 verified; US plan for the owner to enter)
pillars.evidence: At US$679 a month, high-priced lines (CSPX about US$800, CNDX about US$1,560) cannot be bought from one deposit. W46: VWRA left US$110.16 uninvested. All five audits found that the round-1 US$100 bitcoin minimum paid 1.7% in commission.

pillars.name: 15-year all-in cost per deposited dollar (line choice across wrappers)
pillars.definition:
Expected annual cost in bps; lower is better.
Full form: CST10_i = -(TD_ref + G_i) + TAX01_i + 0.5 x TAX03_i + TAX05_i + amortised entry cost + FX for a non-USD line.
- TAX01_i is always the 30% investor-level withholding for US-listed lines. For UCITS lines it is the fund-level look-through, but only when CST02 is missing.
- Entry cost: the CST08 commission share, half the CST04 spread, and residue x r_forgone (0.6% a month) unless fractional shares are confirmed. From 3 owner fills, realised costs from REC05 replace the estimates.
Fallback, one rule for every group (UCITS-only, cross-wrapper, bitcoin and options-income): when CST02 is missing for the group, every line uses TERnow + TAX01 (all levels) + entry cost + FX. The report labels this fallback mode.
A line with a blank TER is not ranked until EVT02 seeds it.
The lowest CST10 among lines passing every gate picks the line, with hysteresis of 5 bps or more at 2 monthly runs. A US-listed line also needs a 10 bps edge over the best eligible non-US line (20 bps in the FIT12 amber band) and FIT12 headroom. The 145 US candidates are added to runs/{week}/v2_line_values.csv so CST10 and the EVT02 trigger run on US lines; until then their CST10 is the fallback computed from universe_us_*.csv yields and TERs. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: Derived from CST01, CST02, CST04, CST08, TAX01, TAX03, TAX05, REC05; yfinance yields (VOO 1.07%, JEPI 7.93%, JEPQ 11.96%, JEPI.L 7.44%, JEPQ.L 11.47%); v2_line_values.csv (UCITS rows: CSPX.L 23.46, VUAA.L 23.26, VWRA.L 24.64)

pillars.name: Withholding drag at every level, by wrapper
pillars.definition:
In bps a year:
(1) Irish physical:
- look-through US weight x US dividend yield x 15% (verified);
- plus non-US weights x yield x the unrecoverable level-1 rate. This component is unverified and recorded at 0 weight until a treaty table is verified and logged.
Irish swap on a qualified index: about 0, with the rule risk in TAX03. Luxembourg physical: 30% on US dividends. Irish ELN premium-income funds: 15% on the US stock dividends only; ELN coupons from non-US banks are assumed to carry no US withholding, and EVT06 watches this. This fund-level part is inactive when CST02 exists for the group.
(2) US-listed: 30% x the trailing 12-month ordinary distribution yield, always active. It includes option-premium and ELN income paid as dividends, plus the fund's unrecoverable foreign withholding on non-US holdings. The yield comes from yfinance's Dividends series only, with duplicate rows removed; the Capital Gains column is excluded because capital-gain distributions carry no withholding for a non-resident alien. Interest-related and short-term-gain dividends under 871(k) are exempted only once REC10 confirms them on IBKR statements or Form 1042-S.
(3) Spot bitcoin and gold trusts, and LSE bitcoin ETPs: 0, since they pay no distributions.
The yield actually received after all withholding is shown next to each US-listed and options-income line. Weight 0.4 of TAX, k = 15 bps.
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV Location column; Vanguard region weights; yfinance Dividends (Capital Gains excluded, de-duplicated) and yield (verified: VWRA 8.97, CSPX 14.79 bps computed); treaty table for non-US look-through (unverified); IBKR 1042-S via REC10
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 3: 30% under IRC 871(a)/1441 with no US-UAE treaty; 15% under the Ireland-US treaty. VOO: 1.07% x 30% = 32 bps, against about 16 bps inside CSPX. JEPI: 7.93% x 30% = 238 bps. JEPQ: 11.96% x 30% = 359 bps. JEPG.L showed 14 payments in 12 months for a monthly payer, hence the de-duplication (data audit).

pillars.name: Tax-rule dependence of a cost advantage
pillars.definition: The part of a line's cost advantage beyond TER that rests on one tax rule, in bps. Examples: 871(m) for swap S&P 500 lines; an 871(k) exemption claimed for a US bond or options-income fund; the assumed absence of US withholding on ELN coupons in Irish premium-income funds; Indian FPI rates; any edge resting on a single treaty article. One-sided: 0 bps scores 50, falling to the floor at 25 bps or more. Half of it is charged in CST10, and S2(c) uses it. EVT06 watches each rule. Weight 0.4 of TAX.
pillars.data_source: justETF replication type (verified); CST02 and TAX01; issuer 871(k) notices (none found yet; JPM 2025 notice lists QDI and 163(j) only); EVT06
pillars.evidence: SPXS and XSPU avoid the 15% withholding through 871(m). Of SPXS's 19.3 bps edge over CSPX, 17.3 bps beyond TER would vanish if the rule changed. Unverified while CST02 is only a raw gap and no 871(k) notice is found.

pillars.name: Distribution friction
pillars.definition: 0 for an accumulating class. For a distributing class, the lower of two costs, in bps a year: one commission per reinvested payment, or the cash drag of yield x average days idle / 365 x r_forgone, with payouts joining the next deposit order. A distributing class is eligible only where its group has no affordable accumulating line. In the options-income sleeve a distributing line is allowed and charged in full; accumulating UCITS options-income classes exist (JEQA.L, JEGA.L, QYLU.L) and score 0. Weight 0.2 of TAX.
pillars.data_source: Universe accumulating column; yfinance Dividends and frequency (de-duplicated)
pillars.evidence: A monthly payer at a 10% yield creates 12 small cash amounts a year that either sit idle or each pay a minimum commission. Every US-listed fund distributes.

pillars.name: Fund size, age and flows
pillars.definition:
- Size (0.6): min(fund AUM, 5 x share-class AUM) in US$, log-scaled from US$50m and saturating at US$5bn.
- Age (0.4): years since the traded line launched, saturating at 5. The issuer or universe date is preferred over yfinance's.
- Flows: 12-month net flows from weekly shares-outstanding snapshots, penalising outflows only. Scored once 52 snapshots exist, recorded until then.
A durability flag (AUM under US$100m with 12-month outflows) stops buying under S2. Weight 0.6 of DUR.
pillars.data_source: iShares net assets; justETF size; yfinance totalAssets and fundInceptionDate (verified for US funds); universe inception column; REC02 snapshot store (flows part, to create)
pillars.evidence: Small, young ETFs close far more often, forcing a switch. Inflows are not rewarded, because flows chase returns (Dannhauser and Pontiff 2019). yfinance gave XNAS a 2026-09 inception against the true 2021-01-21, hence the issuer date.

pillars.name: Custody and counterparty structure (gate for ETCs, bitcoin and ELN income; record for swaps)
pillars.definition:
- Gold ETC gate: allocated, segregated LBMA metal in a non-US vault, a named custodian, and a trustee or security over the metal.
- Bitcoin gate: a named qualified custodian, segregated cold storage, no lending or rehypothecation, authorised-participant creation and redemption, a bankruptcy-remote issuer (for LSE ETNs, secured notes with a security trustee), and a published attestation where offered.
- Options-income gate: fails if one ELN counterparty exceeds 10% of NAV without collateral. The ELN share of NAV is recorded from N-PORT (about 60 days' lag).
- Swap lines and physical funds: counterparties, net swap exposure and share on loan are recorded.
The owner records the gate facts in a new config block: etc_checks and btc_checks {line: {custodian, segregation, security_trustee, attestation_date, checked_on}}. The agent proposes the values with cited sources, and the owner confirms them. Re-checked yearly and on any EVT05 event.
pillars.data_source: Issuer pages, prospectuses, S-1 and 10-K on EDGAR (IBIT prospectus parsed: Coinbase Custody, Anchorage); N-PORT holdings for ELN shares (JEPQ 2026-06-30 parsed); iShares lending table; justETF counterparties (verified); owner etc_checks and btc_checks block (not yet in config)
pillars.evidence: Custody is a total-loss tail risk for bitcoin products (Mt Gox 2014, FTX 2022), and one custodian holds the coins of most US spot ETFs. UCITS rules cap counterparty exposure at 10% of NAV, which sets the comparison. Unverified only because the owner block is missing (data test 6), so no bitcoin or gold line passes until it exists.

pillars.name: Switch-ready substitutes
pillars.definition: Number of other eligible lines in the same ELG07 group with TER within 0.10% and CST10 within 15 bps, using CST10's fallback form when CST02 is missing. A different issuer counts double, and a substitute counts only if it passes ELG08. A US-listed substitute counts only if FIT12 headroom covers the whole position. For a US-listed line, at least one substitute must be non-US-situs (UCITS or an LSE bitcoin ETP) so that S8 can execute. 0 scores worst and 2 or more saturates. Names the S1, S2 and S8 switch target. Weight 0.4 of DUR.
pillars.data_source: Universe after gates; ELG07 groups (approved_equivalents.csv to create); CST01, CST10, ELG08, FIT12
pillars.evidence: S1, S2 and S8 switch into a substitute, never into cash. VWRA's fallbacks (FWRA, ACWD) are blocked until the owner checks them (W46). Round 2 removed the inherited 'fails closed' clause. It remains unverified until approved_equivalents.csv and the ELG08 entries exist.

pillars.name: Beta-consistent expected excess return (FIT04 input)
pillars.definition: E[R_g - R_f] = beta_g x ERP_world (4.0%) + clip(sum_j b_j x (x_gj - x_world,j), -2%, +2%) - (CST10_g - CST10_world)/100, in % a year. beta_g is the FAC05 beta. The b_j are unestimated priors on EXR06, EXR08 and FAC01-FAC04, labelled as such wherever they appear; a missing pillar (EXR06 now) contributes 0. Computed per same-index group. Options-income groups use the parent group's value minus their OPT03 net total-return gap. Bitcoin has none. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: FAC05; EXR06; EXR08; FAC01-FAC04; CST10; config priors
pillars.evidence: REC04: with priors at 0, the tilt variants equal the mix exactly, so any qualification comes from the assumed priors. That is disclosed in every report.

pillars.name: Valuation composite: CAPE, multiples, CMA consensus and country risk (context)
pillars.data_source: yfinance funds_data valuation (verified); Shiller CAPE (cached); FRED DFII10; issuer CMA PDFs via a code-checked agent harvest; Damodaran ctryprem page (verified)
pillars.evidence: CAPE explains about 40% of 10-year US return variance but almost nothing at 1 year (Campbell and Shiller 1998; Asness 2012). It cannot be rebuilt point-in-time for REC04, so it stays context.

pillars.name: Currency valuation (carry recorded)
pillars.definition: The exposure-weighted z-score of each non-USD currency's BIS real effective exchange rate against its expanding mean, with 10 years minimum and 70% coverage of non-USD weight. Inverted so a cheaper currency scores higher, and release-lagged. Weight 0.4 of EXR (8% of X) once built. Until then EXR is scored on EXR08 with the coverage factor c, and REC04 is re-run in that state. Carry (unhedged weight x local minus US short rate) is recorded at weight 0.
pillars.data_source: BIS WS_EER M.R.B CSV (probe not yet passed in this engine; engine_v2/exposure.py sets EXR06 = NaN with 'REER source unverified'); FRED fallbacks; FRED and central-bank short rates
pillars.evidence: Real exchange rates mean-revert over 3-5 years (Rogoff 1996), and currency value is rewarded (Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2013). Relabelled unverified in round 2: the engine does not build it and REPORT_V2 lists it as not built (quant audit). The X configuration is kept for REC04 comparability.

pillars.name: Long-term reversal
pillars.definition: USD total return of the group's reference index from month -60 to month -13 (spliced under ELG07; ^NDX before QQQ), minus the world reference's over the same window, with k = 20 points. Lower past return scores higher. Weight 0.6 of EXR (12% of X). EXR06 + EXR08 + FAC01 are capped at 25% of X.
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly closes with ELG07 splices; ^NDX (verified)
pillars.evidence: Long-horizon reversal across countries (De Bondt and Thaler 1985; Richards 1997; Balvers, Wu and Gilliland 2000). Rebuilt exactly in REC04.

pillars.name: Bond expected return (diversifier sleeve, context)
pillars.definition: Yield to worst minus expected default loss by rating, minus TER, plus Treasury roll-down at the fund's duration, plus hedge carry for a hedged class, in % a year. US-listed bond ETFs also subtract TAX01's 30% unless an 871(k) exemption is confirmed. Ranks bond lines within the owner's diversifier share D and informs the owner's choice of D. Never sets a target.
pillars.data_source: iShares bond pages (YTM and duration embedded: AGGH 4.3 and 6.02); yfinance yield for US bond ETFs (AGG 4.11%, IEF 4.05%); FRED Treasury curve (verified); Moody's default studies (JS shell, manual context only)
pillars.evidence: Starting yield explains most of a bond fund's 5-10 year return. Yield to worst is not yet verified for every issuer, and the default-loss input is manual.

pillars.name: Gold real-price valuation (gold sleeve, context)
pillars.definition: Percentile of the monthly USD gold price deflated by US CPI within its history from 1975-01, release-lagged, shown together with the 10-year TIPS yield. Context for the owner's gold 0-or-5% decision. Never sets a target.
pillars.data_source: World Bank Pink Sheet monthly (verified) or yfinance GC=F; FRED CPIAUCSL, DFII10
pillars.evidence: High real gold prices preceded weak 10-year real gold returns (Erb and Harvey 2013).

pillars.name: Value loading (common factor set)
pillars.definition: HML loading from a 60-month point-in-time Newey-West regression of the group reference index's USD excess return on Ken French Developed Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA_perp and WML. Release-lagged, shrunk by min(1, |t|/2), and scored relative to the world's loading with k = 0.2. Weight 0.12 of FAC (4.8% of X), inside the value-cluster cap.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed 5 factors and momentum (verified); yfinance monthly returns
pillars.evidence: The value premium is long-run positive internationally but weak since 2007 (Fama and French 2012; Israel, Laursen and Richardson 2021).

pillars.name: Profitability loading
pillars.definition: RMW loading from the same regression, shrunk by min(1, |t|/2) and scored relative to the world's. Weight 0.30 of FAC.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed factors; yfinance monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Profitability is rewarded (Novy-Marx 2013; Fama and French 2015), with about a third lost after publication (McLean and Pontiff 2016).

pillars.name: Investment loading, orthogonalised to value
pillars.definition: Loading on CMA_perp: Developed CMA regressed on HML over an expanding window ending at the decision date, residual taken. From the same regression, shrunk and scored relative to the world's. Weight 0.28 of FAC. FAC01/FAC03 is a mandatory REC03 pair.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed factors; yfinance monthly returns
pillars.evidence: CMA is largely spanned by HML (Fama and French 2015), so it is orthogonalised to avoid counting value twice.

pillars.name: Size loading, conditional on quality
pillars.definition: SMB loading, counted only when the RMW loading is 0 or above (otherwise 0), relative to the world's. Weight 0.30 of FAC.
pillars.data_source: Ken French Developed factors; yfinance monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Size works only after controlling for junk (Asness, Frazzini, Israel, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2018).

pillars.name: Single market beta and residual alpha (context)
pillars.definition: The system's one beta: a univariate 120-month Ledoit-Wolf regression of the group reference's monthly USD excess return on the ELG07 world reference, release-lagged. It is the only beta used in EXR02, FIT04, RSK01 and RSK07. Options-income groups get their own beta against their underlying, from their own history (36 months minimum, extended by the ELG07(d) splice and then BXM or BXN), for OPT01 and OPT03. Bitcoin's beta is shown in BTC01 only. Residual alpha and its t-statistic are context. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly returns with ELG07 splices; Ken French market and RF
pillars.evidence: Using one beta source removed the +0.46% a year phantom alpha found in v2 round 3. The unit test (world minus world = 0) stays. Measured betas to the underlying: JEPI 0.55, JEPQ 0.66, QYLD 0.51, XYLD 0.61, SPYI 0.70, QQQI 0.74.

pillars.name: Momentum record: 12-1 and residual
pillars.definition: The group's 12-1 USD return minus the world reference's, and the cumulative residual return over months -12 to -2 from a 36-month regression on world returns. Neutralised when MAC09 shows the momentum-crash state. Weight 0. Logged in REC02 and tested in REC04 as one pre-registered variant. In REC03 it is paired with NWS14 and with N, to catch momentum entering through the news agents. Never a reason to buy outside the mix or to sell (S0).
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly adjusted closes
pillars.evidence: Momentum works before costs (Asness, Moskowitz and Pedersen 2013) but crashes (Daniel and Moskowitz 2016). Here, weekly momentum switching returned 14.42% against 11.85% for holding, but with a -49.7% drawdown and about -6% a year in 2015-2019 (backtest_latest.json).

pillars.name: Excess drawdown path (merged, one-sided)
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly closes with splices; ^NDX; Ken French market series
pillars.evidence: REPORT_V2: Nasdaq-100 +7.9 points in Covid and -6.7 in 2022 beyond beta. v2 used RSK02 and RSK04 only through RSK01, so making them components leaves X unchanged (confirmed against exposure.py).

pillars.name: Downside-upside beta asymmetry (one-sided)
pillars.definition: Beta to the world in down months minus beta in up months, over 120 months, point-in-time. Only asymmetry above the world's is penalised (k = 0.2). Weight 0.35 of RSK.
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Downside beta is priced and painful (Ang, Chen and Xing 2006), and correlations rise in falls (Longin and Solnik 2001).

pillars.name: Tail fatness (one-sided)
pillars.definition: Monthly 95% CVaR divided by monthly volatility over 120 months, against the world's (k = 0.5). Only fatter tails are penalised. Weight 0.30 of RSK.
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly returns
pillars.evidence: Volatility understates crash risk for skewed exposures, and short-volatility overlays have fat left tails (Kelly and Jiang 2014).

pillars.name: Portfolio drawdown budget (constraint)
pillars.definition: Replays the target mix after the order through every listed stress window that ended at least 1 month before the date: 2008-09, 2011, 2020 Q1, 2022, and also 2018 for bitcoin. It includes the bitcoin sleeve (BTC-USD from 2014, short history disclosed) and any options-income sleeve (own history extended under ELG07(d)). The worst loss minus the world's worst must be 5 points or less for any score-driven tilt; tilts are scaled down until it holds. For the owner's mix the result is shown, not enforced. Also shows the current drawdown of the mix and the world from their highs. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly returns; BTC-USD; Cboe BXM/BXN (curl -L); positions
pillars.evidence: REPORT_V2: mix -24.6% against world -24.3% over 10 years (budget -29.3%). GOAL success measure: worst drawdown against the world.

pillars.name: Risk-contribution ratio (constraint)
pillars.definition: Each sleeve's share of portfolio variance (120-month Ledoit-Wolf covariance; bitcoin on its available history with shrinkage) divided by its capital weight, at target weights. Limit 1.5 for equity, gold and bond sleeves. The owner-sized bitcoin sleeve is exempt from blocking: its ratio (about 2 to 4 at 5%) and risk share are always shown with a speculative warning, and FIT13 is the binding limit. Weight 0.
pillars.data_source: yfinance monthly returns; BTC-USD, IBIT
pillars.evidence: REPORT_V2 ratios: world 0.98, S&P 500 1.0, Nasdaq-100 1.17. Capital weights hide risk concentration (Qian 2005). The bitcoin figure checks out at about 2.5 for volatility of 70 against 15 and correlation 0.4 (quant audit).

pillars.name: Look-through composition: breadth, country, currency, sector and concentration (context)
pillars.data_source: iShares holdings CSV (blackrock.com/uk ajax); Vanguard region table; ELG07 stand-ins; US issuer holdings files and SEC N-PORT; snapshot store
pillars.evidence: Concentration adds unrewarded risk. In v2 all three merged pillars were weight-0 readings of the same holdings files.

pillars.name: Restricted-market exposure (gate)
pillars.definition: Look-through weight in markets listed in config/restricted_markets.csv. Each row carries a primary-source citation and date, added by EVT07 and checked by code. Above 5%, the line cannot receive deposits. Until the file exists, CON04 is listed as missing in every report. It is not applied as a block, because no rows exist and current index weights in previously sanctioned markets are 0. EVT07 severity 3 still blocks lines directly. Weight 0.
