pillars.data_source: Holdings Location column; SEC N-PORT for US funds; config/restricted_markets.csv (not yet created)
pillars.evidence: Russia 2022: frozen holdings were written down. Relabelled unverified in round 2 because the config file does not exist (portfolio audit).

pillars.name: Specialised or thematic hype (line gate)
pillars.definition: Flag 1 for a narrow thematic, single-industry or single-frontier-country fund launched within 5 years or after a top-quintile 36-month index return. Flag 0.5 for other narrow sector or theme funds; 0 for broad funds. Flag 1 blocks deposits; 0.5 is a warning. Applies equally to US-listed themes (the 17 theme rows in universe_us_core.csv) and to narrow-theme options-income lines (for example FEPI, FEPI.L, YMAG.L, CHPY.L). Spot bitcoin is excluded, because FIT13 governs it.
pillars.data_source: Universe type and inception columns; yfinance category, inception and index history
pillars.evidence: Specialised ETFs underperform by about 6% a year over the 5 years after launch (Ben-David, Franzoni, Kim and Moussawi 2023).

pillars.name: Upside given up
pillars.definition:
Up-capture U is the line's geometric mean return in months when the underlying rose, divided by the underlying's, over the line's full history (36 months minimum, extended under ELG07(d): US-twin gross history first, then the Cboe proxy, labelled). OPT01 is the mean of two parts:
(a) U against the plain buy-write of the same underlying: d = U - U_proxy, with U_proxy = 0.56 for BXM (S&P 500 writers) and 0.44 for BXN (Nasdaq-100 writers), recomputed yearly. Global writers use their own history against the world underlying. k = 0.30, so a line that keeps more upside than a plain buy-write scores above 50;
(b) upside given up beyond the beta reduction: U - beta (FAC05 beta to the underlying), k = 0.10. This penalises a line that gives up more upside than its lower beta explains.
Also shown: capture in the underlying's strongest rolling 12 months, and the share of months above +3% in which the line lagged by more than 2 points. Weight 0.40 of O.
pillars.data_source: yfinance adjusted closes of JEPI, JEPQ, XYLD, QYLD, SPYI, QQQI and the UCITS options-income lines and their underlyings (verified); cdn.cboe.com BXM and BXN history fetched with curl -L (verified 2026-11-13)

pillars.name: Net income relative to peers, and its quality
pillars.definition:
Net income yield = trailing 12-month distribution yield (yfinance Dividends only, de-duplicated, capital gains excluded) x (1 - investor-level withholding) - TAX05. Investor-level withholding is 30% on US-listed lines and 0 on Irish UCITS. For an accumulating class, the distributing twin's gross yield is used, with no withholding. The yield is adjusted down for:
- the share paid as return of capital (from US 19a-1 notices or UCITS reports);
- unstable payouts, when the coefficient of variation of the last 12-24 payments is above 0.3.
Scored against the median net income yield of eligible options-income lines on the same underlying (not against the index's dividend yield), with k = 3 points. Income counts as return only through OPT03, because the owner accumulates and pays no UAE income tax. Weight 0.25 of O.
pillars.data_source: yfinance Dividends and yield (verified: JEPI 7.93%, JEPQ 11.96%, JEPI.L 7.44%, JEPG.L 7.79%, JEPQ.L 11.47%, QYLD.L 12.15%); TAX01; issuer 19a-1 and UCITS annual reports (the return-of-capital part is recorded until verified)
pillars.better_when: higher net income than peers, more stable
pillars.evidence: Owner requirement 4: scored on income. Against the index dividend yield every line saturated near 100 (quant audit), so it is now scored against peers. On the S&P 500 underlying, JEPI nets 7.93% x 0.7 = 5.55%, against 7.44% for JEPI.L. On the Nasdaq-100, JEPQ nets 8.37% against 11.47% for JEPQ.L. The withholding gap separates the wrappers.

pillars.name: Beta-adjusted downside cushion and net total-return gap
pillars.definition:
Over the same window as OPT01 (with the same proxy rule), the mean of two parts:
(a) beta-adjusted downside: down-capture minus the FAC05 beta to the underlying, lower is better, two-sided, k = 0.10. Raw down-capture is no longer scored, because low beta alone would earn it;
(b) net total-return gap: the annualised total return after TAX01 at every level and after CST01, minus a beta-matched mix (beta x underlying plus (1 - beta) x T-bills), with k = 2 points a year. A positive gap means the overlay added value beyond its lower beta.
Shown alongside: the raw gap against the underlying, the maximum-drawdown ratio, NAV erosion (price-return drift), and an asymmetry flag when down-capture exceeds up-capture. Weight 0.35 of O. Also feeds EXR02 for options-income groups.

allocation_method:
Allocation runs monthly; the weekly run never moves money. The owner's mix routes the deposit, the caps and gates shape the order, and scores and news only advise until a gate passes.

1. Cash. C = 2,500 AED / 3.6725 - US$2 FX minimum = US$678.74. Carried cash, residue and distributions received net of withholding are added. If the MAC05 peg flag is on, conversion goes through the cheapest available channel (EVT08). The deposit is never skipped. Batching over k = 1 or 2 months is unchanged from v2.

2. Sleeves and targets (config/portfolio_v2.yaml; every change logged in CHANGELOG).
- Current file: world 70 (VWRA, then FWRA and ACWD as fallbacks once the owner has checked them), S&P 500 20, Nasdaq-100 10.
- Bitcoin, per 'bitcoin in at 5%': strategic_mix.bitcoin target 0.05, labelled speculative, hard cap 5% (FIT13). The other sleeves scale pro rata to world 66.5, S&P 500 19, Nasdaq-100 9.5 unless the owner writes another split. This is an owner mix change, not a tested rule. The owner may instead set a target of 4.5% to reduce trim churn; the cap stays 5% either way.
- Options-income, per 'options-income in': its lines enter the universe as candidates. The options_income sleeve target stays 0 until the owner answers an explicit prompt in the weekly report and CHANGELOG. The prompt asks for:
(i) the target (a 10% ceiling is proposed, not owner-set);
(ii) the underlying (S&P 500 premium income, Nasdaq-100 premium income, or global);
(iii) which sleeve it is carved from.
REC07 variant (b) is shown beside the prompt: BXM trailed the S&P 500 by 3.75 points a year and BXN trailed the Nasdaq-100 by 10.2.
- Gold (0 or 5%) and bonds (D of 0-20%) remain owner choices. Any satellite is 0% or at least 5%, except bitcoin, which is at most 5%.
- Config edits to make before the first v3 run, for the owner to confirm:
 - strategic_mix.bitcoin {target 0.05, label speculative} and options_income {target 0, underlying null, carved_from null};
 - positions_as_of 2026-11-13 (a zero start);
 - orderable migrated to the dict schema, with entries for BTCW.L, IB1T.L, IBIT, JEPI.L, JEPQ.L, JEQA.L, JEGA.L and QYLU.L for the owner to check in TWS;
 - ibkr_entity, w8ben_signed_on and us_commission_plan;
 - the etc_checks and btc_checks blocks.

3. Gaps (FIT01). g_s = target_s x (V + C) - value_s, where V is the portfolio value from the fills ledger. positions {} with positions_as_of is a valid zero start. Only positions with no as_of date, or one older than 35 days, send the deposit to the world line.

4. Order.
- All cash goes in one order to the sleeve with the largest positive gap whose best line passes every gate and can take an order of at least US$340.
- A capped sleeve's order is cut to its headroom: bitcoin to the FIT13 room, a US-listed order to the FIT12 room. If that headroom is below US$340, the sleeve is skipped this month and its gap is carried.
- If an order is cut and US$340 or more is left over, the remainder goes to the next-largest gap as a second order in the same session. A smaller remainder is carried as cash into next month's C.
- Otherwise a second order is placed only if cash exceeds one order by US$680 or more.
- At most 2 orders, each at least US$340, so the US$1.70 commission stays at or below 0.5% (CST08).
- If no line in the sleeve passes, the money goes to the next gap and finally to VWRA. The deposit is never skipped.

5. Structural events first. Any EVT01, EVT02 or EVT05 at severity 2 or more, EVT07 at severity 3, or a gate failure blocks that line at once. The group's next eligible line takes the order.

6. Line choice inside the sleeve's same-index group. The lowest CST10 among lines passing every gate wins, using the fallback (TERnow + TAX01 + entry) wherever CST02 is missing. A challenger must lead by 5 bps or more at 2 monthly runs, each on the median of 4 weekly readings (hysteresis). The old line is frozen and still counts toward FIT11's 6-line limit.
A US-listed line may win only if all three hold:
(a) its CST10, including 30% investor withholding on all ordinary distributions, is at least 10 bps a year lower than the best eligible non-US line (20 bps in FIT12's amber band), or the group has no orderable non-US line;
(b) V_us after the order is at or below US$54,000;
(c) ELG08 confirms US-ETF access, ibkr_entity and a valid W-8BEN.
Cap space is scarce. Over time it goes to the line with the largest saving in bps per dollar, and first to exposures with no non-US alternative.
Results on 2026-11-13 inputs:
- the world, S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 sleeves stay UCITS: VT about 53 against VWRA 24.6; VOO about 35 against CSPX 23.5; QQQM about 29 against XNAS 33.4, a 4 bps edge inside the hurdle;
- options-income goes UCITS: JEPI about 273 against JEPI.L about 55; JEPQ about 394 against JEPQ.L about 45.
The US$60,000 headroom therefore serves mainly US-only exposures and, if needed, a US spot bitcoin ETF.

7. Bitcoin (FIT13). It is owner-sized, never in X, and never score-, tilt- or news-sized.
- Money arrives only through gap routing toward the 5% target, in orders of at least US$340 sized so that B after the order is at most 5%. A smaller gap is carried. Below a portfolio of about US$6,800 there is no bitcoin buy, and the report says so.
- Warning at 4.5%; no buys at 5% or above.
- At each month-end check, after the deposit has been routed elsewhere, B above 5.0% is trimmed to 4.5% (S7).
- Line: a physically backed LSE ETP (ELG01 class e, a secured ETN, for example BTCW.L in USD) that passes DUR02 and ELG08, has a TER seeded from its KID, and is cleared by the owner's crypto-ETP permission. It is preferred because it uses no US headroom and carries no US estate exposure. A US spot ETF is chosen only if its CST10 is at least 15 bps lower and it fits FIT12, or if no LSE ETP is orderable for the owner's IBKR entity.
- Until a bitcoin line is orderable and btc_checks exist, the bitcoin gap is routed to the next gap, and each month's report shows what the owner must do.
- A 5% bitcoin sleeve held through a US ETF alone would reach US$60,000 only at about a US$1.2m portfolio.

8. Options-income. Deposits go to it only when the owner has set a target and underlying.
- The line is chosen within the owner's chosen ELG07 group: S&P 500 premium income {JEPI, JEPI.L}, Nasdaq-100 premium income {JEPQ, JEPQ.L, JEQA.L}, global {JEPG.L, JEGA.L}, or Nasdaq-100 BuyWrite {QYLD, QYLD.L, QYLU.L}.
- The winner is the line with the highest O among gate-passing lines whose O is at least the O of the plain buy-write proxy, with CST10 as the tie-break. In practice the UCITS lines (JEPI.L, JEPQ.L, and the accumulating JEQA.L and JEGA.L) win, because US lines lose about 2.4-3.6 points a year to withholding.
- It is never a same-index substitute inside the S&P 500 or Nasdaq-100 sleeves. It counts as its underlying in FIT07, FIT08 and FIT11. With the mix already near its US limit, a US-heavy target is shown as an owner warning.
- The distributing class is allowed and charged through TAX05.

9. Never bought: information-only types under ELG03 (leveraged, inverse, single-stock including single-stock option-income, ULTY, YMAX, buffer, SVOL and other volatility products, futures-crypto, and BTCI), and US partnerships and unsecured ETNs under ELG01.

10. Scores and news. X and fit tilts may route money only after REC04 passes, re-run against the new mix; news tilts only after REC08's primary test passes. Tilts are then limited to 10% per sleeve and 15% in total (score and news tilts share this), at most 2 of any 12 deposits, never into bitcoin or options-income, within FIT07, FIT08, FIT10 (3% or less), RSK06 and RSK07, and each needs the owner's confirmation. FIT12 and FIT13 always bind.

11. Execution. EVT09 picks the order day (a delay of 1 week at most). Ladder: limit at mid plus a quarter of the spread, then mid plus half, then the ask; at mid under MAC03 caution. LSE 14:30-16:15 London; US 10:00-15:30 New York. Whole shares on the LSE; fractional shares on US lines where ELG08 confirms them. If the cheapest line does not fit in whole shares, the next line within 10 bps is used. Every rung, fill, carry and delay is logged in REC02 and REC05.

12. Weekly report. It shows:
- the FIT12 gauge (V_us against 45k, 54k and 60k);
- the FIT13 gauge (B against 4.5% and 5%, plus the last trim);
- the options-income prompt until the owner answers, and then the options-income share;
- FIT07 headroom;
- the information-only watch table;
- coverage and missing or unverified pillars;
- the list of owner actions still blocking bitcoin, US-listed and options-income orders.

- config/universe_us_core.csv: 112 US-listed rows, all yfinance-verified. By type: broad US 16, world 3, ex-US 7, EM 5, factor 11, dividend 7, sector 16, themes 17 (AI, semis, cyber, defence, clean energy), bonds 17, gold 4, bitcoin 3, options-income 6.

US buy-candidate count. There are 168 unique US tickers after de-duplicating 9 that appear in both files. 23 are information-only:
- 15 leveraged;
- 4 single-stock option-income (TSLY, NVDY, MSTY, CONY);
- 4 added in round 2: BTCI (bitcoin-linked option income, which would escape the 5% cap), SVOL (short VIX futures), YMAX (a fund of single-stock option-income ETFs) and ULTY (option income on a handful of single stocks).
That leaves 145 US-listed buy candidates. This is a small deviation from 'about 150'; the reason is that owner requirement 4 forbids buying these four. Gates remove further lines on each run, for example BIL, SGOV and SHY under ELG04.
Each line gets an ELG01 class, an ELG03 type, an ELG04 sleeve and an ELG07 group keyed on declared benchmark identity. US lines join the existing UCITS groups where the index matches, so VOO, IVV, SPY, SPYM, CSPX, VUAA and SPXS are one S&P 500 exposure, scored once. Membership is confirmed by a monthly return check, not a weekly one: weekly correlations across London and New York stay near 0.93 even for identical indices. New groups appear only for exposures with no UCITS twin. Narrow-theme options-income lines (FEPI, FEPI.L, YMAG.L, CHPY.L) fall under the CON05 gate.

Costs priced in.
- US-listed: TAX01 always charges 30% investor-level withholding on every ordinary distribution, since there is no US-UAE treaty (IRC 871(a), 1441). This includes option-premium and ELN income paid as dividends, plus the fund's unrecoverable foreign withholding on non-US holdings. Yields come from yfinance Dividends only, de-duplicated; capital-gain distributions are excluded, because a non-resident alien pays no withholding on them.
- 871(k) interest-related and short-term-gain exemptions count only after REC10 confirms them on IBKR statements or Form 1042-S, and are marked as rule dependence in TAX03.
- Irish UCITS: 15% on US dividends at fund level (Ireland-US treaty), measured once in CST02, or as look-through in TAX01 while CST02 is missing; 0 at investor level. The non-US look-through component is unverified until a treaty table is verified.
- Irish ELN premium-income funds: 15% on the stock dividends; ELN coupons are assumed free of US withholding, a rule dependence watched by EVT06.
- Luxembourg physical: 30%. Irish swap: about 0, plus half of the 871(m) edge as rule risk.
- Spot bitcoin trusts, LSE bitcoin ETPs and gold trusts: no distributions, so no withholding. US trusts are still US-situs.
